analysis: Docs-only change in docs/architecture/inference.md. The changed head ranges are 619-625, 869-905 and 1767. Units 8 and 9 show head lines 416-1234. Lines 619-625 describe EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate. Age and expiry stay anchored to the newest observation, so an older out-of-order receipt cannot move freshness backward, and a heartbeat snapshot never renews evidence. Lines 869-905 describe three TTFT admission estimator corrections, with a rollback switch DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift): per-step decode pricing via CBv2DecodeRateShape with MTP depth-gate mirroring; reviewed deadline-calibrated requests that keep the per-row 1+k charge; and an idle-calibration floor on the isolated prefill rate, at least 1/8 of the calibration rate, with evidence older than 30 minutes on an idle engine treated as absent. These are admission and deadline performance estimators. They do not touch the threat-model assets: encryption (T-008), cache scope or salt (T-041/SEC-035), attestation or authorization (TB-011, T-052..T-058), or billing. Actual deadline expiry, memory admission and physical KV reservation are documented as unchanged (lines 867-868, 919-920). A less conservative estimate could admit requests that later miss their deadlines. That is an availability/QoS tradeoff that remains bounded by actual elapsed expiry; it is not a security regression. Surrounding Super-slot text (cache scope partitioning at line 509, no cache receipts) appears unchanged. Head line 1767 falls outside the supplied units, so that change is not examined. The implementing Swift sources are not supplied. Integration may confirm that the rollback environment key is treated as performance-affecting by DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification (line 935). No findings.
